findings.summary: Homeostatically regulated recurrent-network literature treats external input as a separate control variable that can sustain population spiking while placing the recurrent network in a different dynamical regime. Aggregate nonzero activity therefore does not establish recurrent/internal liveness.
sources: Zierenberg, Wilting & Priesemann, Physical Review X 2018, DOI 10.1103/PhysRevX.8.031018

findings.summary: The reverberating branching-model literature explicitly decomposes afferent external activation from recurrent internal activation, with external fraction h/<A> = 1-m in the model. This supplies an ordinary conceptual baseline for source-stratified liveness rather than one all-field dead flag.

Homeostatic plasticity spans neuron-own firing-rate sensing, local adaptation, cell-autonomous scaling/structural plasticity and network-wide regulation. Pooling receptor and reservoir units under one target, denominator and liveness detector is therefore not a canonical consequence of homeostasis and should be an explicit contract choice.
sources: Turrigiano, Cold Spring Harbor Perspectives in Biology 2012, DOI 10.1101/cshperspect.a005736
Lu et al., eLife Version of Record 2025-07-04, DOI 10.7554/eLife.88376.3

findings.summary: Firing-rate recovery and correlation/network-structure recovery can depend on different homeostatic mechanisms and recover independently. A single dead boolean or active-unit fraction therefore should not be interpreted as generic network stability without a named observable contract.
